issue.title: `---` after a link reference definition becomes a paragraph instead of a thematic break
issue.body:
A line of dashes (`---`) immediately following a link reference definition is rendered by md4c as a paragraph (`

---

`) instead of a thematic break (`
`). input: ``` markdown [f]:r --- ``` cmark output: ``` html
``` md4c ouput: ``` html

---

``` input: ``` markdown [foo]: /url --- [foo] ``` cmark output: ``` html

foo

``` md4c output: ``` html

--- foo

``` This is specific to `---`. Other thematic breaks—`***`, `___`, and spaced variants `- - -`/`_ _ _`—after a refdef are all correctly rendered as `
`.

issue.title: Feature request: optional flag to preserve extra blank lines
issue.body:
### Summary Add an **opt-in** parser flag that preserves consecutive blank lines from the source, exposing each *extra* blank line as a new lightweight block type in the callback stream. This is intended for WYSIWYG-style consumers (editors, mobile renderers that build their own view tree from the MD4C callbacks) where the number of blank lines the user typed is meaningful and should survive into the output. It is deliberately non-CommonMark and therefore gated behind a flag; with the flag off, behaviour and output are unchanged. ### Motivation / use case We consume the MD4C callback stream directly (not the HTML renderer) to build a native view tree on iOS/Android, aiming for a WYSIWYG-ish experience. In CommonMark, any run of blank lines between two blocks collapses to a single block separator, so a user who typed three empty lines between two paragraphs sees the same result as one empty line - the vertical spacing they intentionally added is lost. The information is discarded very early: in `md_process_line()`, a blank line simply ends the current block, and consecutive blanks are no-ops. Nothing about the *count* of blank lines ever reaches a callback, so this cannot be recovered by a downstream consumer or a custom renderer - the only workaround today is to pre-process the Markdown string (forcing empty paragraphs) before handing it to the parser, which every consumer has to reimplement and which is easy to get wrong around fenced code, lists, etc. Exposing it natively (as an opt-in) lets consumers who want WYSIWYG semantics get them without string hacks, while everyone else is unaffected. ### Proposed design - New flag `MD_FLAG_PRESERVEBLANKLINES` (`0x400000`). - New block type `MD_BLOCK_BLANK`, appended at the end of `MD_BLOCKTYPE` (so no existing enum values shift). It carries **no contents** (no `MD_TEXT` is emitted) and has `NULL` detail — an `ENTER`/`LEAVE` pair a renderer can turn into a spacer. - Semantics for a run of *N* consecutive blank lines: the **first** blank keeps its usual role as the CommonMark block separator (not emitted); each **subsequent** blank emits one `MD_BLOCK_BLANK`. So *N* blanks → *N − 1* preserved blocks, matching the empty-paragraph workaround. - **Leading** blank lines (before any block has been buffered) are suppressed. **Trailing** blanks are preserved. Blanks inside containers (list items, block quotes) nest correctly, because the blank block is pushed into the same buffered block stream as the container open/close markers. ### Example Input: ``` Paragraph one. Paragraph two. ``` Callback stream **with** the flag (schematically): ``` ENTER P → TEXT "Paragraph one." → LEAVE P ENTER BLANK → LEAVE BLANK (extra blank #1) ENTER BLANK → LEAVE BLANK (extra blank #2) ENTER P → TEXT "Paragraph two." → LEAVE P ``` With the flag **off**: identical to today (one `P`, one `P`). The bundled `md4c-html` renderer, for demonstration, renders each `MD_BLOCK_BLANK` as `

 

`. ### Verification - Full CommonMark suite (`test/run-testsuite.py -s test/spec.txt`): **652 passed, 0 failed** with the flag off — default output is byte-for-byte unchanged. - Verified the new behaviour both at the raw `MD_PARSER` callback level and via `md_html(...)`. - Sanity-checked edge cases: leading blanks (suppressed), trailing blanks (preserved), blanks between list items, blanks inside block quotes. ### Open questions for maintainers 1. Is an opt-in, non-CommonMark flag like this acceptable in the core, or would you prefer it live only as documentation of the pre-processing approach? 2. Preferred representation: a new `MD_BLOCK_BLANK` type (as here), vs. reusing an empty `MD_BLOCK_P`, vs. a single block carrying a *count* in a detail struct? 3. Leading/trailing-blank policy (currently: suppress leading, keep trailing). Is that the behaviour you'd want? 4. Interaction with list looseness (tight vs. loose) deserves dedicated spec tests before this would be merge-ready; happy to add a `test/spec-preserve-blank-lines.txt` if the direction is welcome. I'm attaching a working proof-of-concept patch below (against `0.5.3` / 9de89d8). It's ~33 lines across `md4c.h`, `md4c.c`, and `md4c-html.c`. Happy to turn it into a proper PR with tests and CLI wiring if you're open to the feature. _Note: I'm not sure what's your approach on this, but this patch was AI generated and then verified by me_
Proof-of-concept patch (git apply-able) ```diff diff --git a/src/md4c-html.c b/src/md4c-html.c index 590078d..0d11c4d 100644 --- a/src/md4c-html.c +++ b/src/md4c-html.c @@ -452,6 +452,7 @@ enter_block_callback(MD_BLOCKTYPE type, void* detail, void* userdata) case MD_BLOCK_FOOTNOTE_DEF_SECTION: RENDER_VERBATIM(r, "
\n
    \n"); break; case MD_BLOCK_FOOTNOTE_DEF: render_open_footnote_def_block(r, (MD_BLOCK_FOOTNOTE_DEF_DETAIL*)detail); break; case MD_BLOCK_ADMONITION: render_open_admonition_block(r, (const MD_BLOCK_ADMONITION_DETAIL*) detail); break; + case MD_BLOCK_BLANK: RENDER_VERBATIM(r, "

    \xc2\xa0

    \n"); break; } return 0; @@ -483,6 +484,7 @@ leave_block_callback(MD_BLOCKTYPE type, void* detail, void* userdata) case MD_BLOCK_FOOTNOTE_DEF_SECTION: RENDER_VERBATIM(r, "
\n
\n"); break; case MD_BLOCK_FOOTNOTE_DEF: render_close_footnote_def_block(r, (MD_BLOCK_FOOTNOTE_DEF_DETAIL*)detail); break; case MD_BLOCK_ADMONITION: RENDER_VERBATIM(r, "\n"); break; + case MD_BLOCK_BLANK: /* noop (whole block emitted on enter) */ break; } return 0; diff --git a/src/md4c.c b/src/md4c.c index 833c074..3a72b5c 100644 --- a/src/md4c.c +++ b/src/md4c.c @@ -5502,7 +5502,8 @@ md_process_leaf_block(MD_CTX* ctx, MD_BLOCK* block) /* Process the block contents accordingly to is type. */ switch(block->type) { case MD_BLOCK_HR: - /* noop */ + case MD_BLOCK_BLANK: + /* noop (no contents) */ break; case MD_BLOCK_CODE: @@ -6988,6 +6989,26 @@ md_process_line(MD_CTX* ctx, const MD_LINE_ANALYSIS** p_pivot_line, MD_LINE_ANAL /* Blank line ends current leaf block. */ if(line->type == MD_LINE_BLANK) { MD_CHECK(md_end_current_block(ctx)); + + /* Optionally preserve extra blank lines for WYSIWYG-like consumers. + * Within a run of consecutive blank lines, the first blank acts as the + * usual CommonMark block separator (not preserved). Every subsequent + * blank in the run (pivot is already the dummy blank line) emits one + * empty MD_BLOCK_BLANK. Leading blank lines (before any content has been + * buffered) are suppressed. */ + if((ctx->parser.flags & MD_FLAG_PRESERVEBLANKLINES) && + *p_pivot_line == &md_dummy_blank_line && + ctx->n_block_bytes > 0) + { + MD_BLOCK* block = (MD_BLOCK*) md_push_block_bytes(ctx, sizeof(MD_BLOCK)); + if(block == NULL) + return -1; + block->type = MD_BLOCK_BLANK; + block->flags = 0; + block->data = 0; + block->n_lines = 0; + } + *p_pivot_line = &md_dummy_blank_line; return 0; } diff --git a/src/md4c.h b/src/md4c.h index e649059..8cddd92 100644 --- a/src/md4c.h +++ b/src/md4c.h @@ -118,7 +118,14 @@ typedef enum MD_BLOCKTYPE { /* Adminition extension. * Detail MD_BLOCK_ADMONITION_DETAIL. * Note: Recognized only when MD_FLAG_ADMONITIONS is enabled. */ - MD_BLOCK_ADMONITION + MD_BLOCK_ADMONITION, + + /* An extra blank (empty) line preserved from the source, beyond the single + * blank line CommonMark uses as a block separator. One such block is emitted + * per extra blank line in a run. It carries no contents (no MD_TEXT is sent) + * and has NULL detail. + * Note: Emitted only when MD_FLAG_PRESERVEBLANKLINES is enabled. */ + MD_BLOCK_BLANK } MD_BLOCKTYPE; /* Span represents an in-line piece of a document which should be rendered with @@ -389,6 +396,7 @@ typedef struct MD_BLOCK_FOOTNOTE_DEF_DETAIL { #define MD_FLAG_ADMONITIONS 0x80000 /* Enable admonitions extension. */ #define MD_FLAG_FOOTNOTES 0x100000 /* Enable [^label] footnote references. */ #define MD_FLAG_HIGHLIGHT 0x200000 /* Enable ==highlight== spans. */ +#define MD_FLAG_PRESERVEBLANKLINES 0x400000 /* Preserve extra blank lines as MD_BLOCK_BLANK (non-CommonMark; for WYSIWYG). */ #define MD_FLAG_PERMISSIVEAUTOLINKS (MD_FLAG_PERMISSIVEEMAILAUTOLINKS | MD_FLAG_PERMISSIVEURLAUTOLINKS | MD_FLAG_PERMISSIVEWWWAUTOLINKS) #define MD_FLAG_NOHTML (MD_FLAG_NOHTMLBLOCKS | MD_FLAG_NOHTMLSPANS) ```
